title: Why Apple's 30% App Store tax hurts users and developers: Durov's 7-point case
summary: Durov argues that Apple's 30% commission on app sales is a platform-level tax that raises prices, forces ad-based business models, kills marginal apps and erodes privacy. It's a lesson in how platform fees distort pricing, product quality and which business models survive.

principles.text: A platform commission stacks on top of every other cost, so it can make otherwise viable products unprofitable.
principles.quote: Many apps would have been net profitable in a world without Apple’s 30% commission, but being forced to surrender 30% of their revenue to Apple makes them unsustainable.

principles.text: A high platform cut pushes developers away from selling services toward ads and selling user data.
principles.quote: Because Apple makes selling premium services and accepting donations one-third less meaningful for developers, many of them have to show ads in their apps in order for their companies to survive.

principles.text: Platform fees get passed to customers as higher prices, so users pay twice (device plus every app).
principles.quote: Apple’s 30% commission makes all apps and digital goods more expensive for you.

principles.text: Money taken as platform tax is money not reinvested in product quality and R&D.
principles.quote: Billions of dollars are taken from developers who could have otherwise spent those funds on improving the quality of the apps you use every day.

principles.text: A gatekeeper's control over distribution means slow review cycles and delayed releases, even for big apps.
principles.quote: Apple’s review team is notoriously inefficient and often delays approval for no apparent reason.

principles.text: Privacy-friendly business models (selling extra services to users) are healthier than data-driven ones, and platform policy decides which one wins.
principles.quote: Apple’s policies skew the entire industry towards selling user data instead of letting them adopt more privacy-friendly business models like selling additional services to their users.
